posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
I've decided to join the herd and start doing Let's Play videos of some of the community's games. My channel is small and right now just consists of a devlog, a trailer, and game test footage, but I'm aiming to change that. This will primarily be for the dev's benefit, as I am not monetized and this takes away from game dev time, in the hopes they can improve their game.
Spoiler:
Who am I?
So, who am I and why should you care? You probably shouldn't, I'm just another random rpg maker dev, but I've been around for a few years and picked up a few things along the way. I've also been a gamer for longer than some of you have been alive. Everything is just my subjective opinion and I'll just call it as I see it. As a dev, I've always really appreciated videos of my games being played and found it really useful to get feedback and find ways to improve my game making skills.
Anywho, right now I'm playing some games that I thought looked cool or interesting for roughly about an hour. The devs didn't request a video or anything, I just wanted to do it for fun. Right now there's a "score" at the end but it doesn't mean anything and is completely arbitrary.
You can request me to play your game but it doesn't mean I will.
Spoiler:
Criteria
I'm doing this for fun, if it doesn't seem like I am going to have fun with your game, I'm not going to play it.
YouTube appropriate - No Adult/sexual content, self harm, excessive swearing (some is fine), nudity, keep it pg-13ish
Polish - a few placeholders are fine but a general amount of polish and detail need to be present. RTP is fine but needs to be used well.
Demos/Early Access etc are fine but it must have roughly an hour's worth of gameplay and meet the above standards.
Mainly Commercial games will be accepted. Exclusions will apply.
No Visual Novels - sorry, I'm not reading your novel.
No AI art/music/programming - it is what it is and not open for discussion
itch.io/steam links only
provide key(s) if your game cost money
First up is
MARGO - On The Brink
by
@SomaelCK
I really enjoyed playing this game. It's very beautiful, and a lot of fun.

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
Long over due for a new Unsolicited Let's Play!
Today I'm checking out Mechanical Throb. Weird title, I know. This game has absolutely gorgeous pixel art and some neat world building. The busts, character sprites, and maps are just absolutely adorable. It's got some good music, there's rtp sounds and some tiles here and there but it's all used rather well.
While there's no spelling errors, the dialogue really needs to be gone over by a editor/translator. There's an over abundant use of ellipsis, if you can even call them that since they're 6 dots long instead of 3. There's several times where there are 3 or more dialogue boxes just full of them. I started having a little bit of fun with it by making fart noises everytime they showed up which was a lot. There's quite a few lines that need to be rewritten as they don't make much sense.
Another big error is pronouns. I believe one of the main characters is a girl/woman but is referred to as he/him throughout the demo. (Edited: after speaking with the dev, it is in fact male, so my bad) And another time when they are talking about a possible "daughter, sister, or nephew" which should be niece. I understand that English is not their first language, so an editor or translator would really be beneficial.
All that said, it's a really well put together puzzle game with charming aesthetics.

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
Finishing up Dungeon Rummage Origins. Nicely done demo! I had an issue with my controller on my end that I didn't get cleared up until halfway through the video, my bad. This game has balanced and engaging combat with well done tight and snappy action sequences. Great little rewards for exploration. I don't think there's a map without a chest or something to check out. The story gets better and more intriguing the longer I got into the game. The story has a mix of mystery and the classic hero's journey. The characters are interesting enough, Dunstan is our young every man. Thaz is a tough take no prisoners orc lady and Allannia is a dutiful mage working for the king. Thaz personality really shines in her dialogue and has the best characterization in the demo. Allannia is a little flat by comparison and I would imagine further in the game we'll learn more about her.
I think buying flat upgrades to the characters instead of gear and levels is an interesting concept. The demo was well balanced and even though I came close to being wiped out, I never felt like the fights were too hard or unfair. Dunstan did get ko'd and I wasn't able to revive him with the revival items, so I guess that's a bug.
This is all nitpicking stuff and just some thoughts:
I wouldn't mind getting Thaz as a party member just a tad bit earlier, like for instance with the bandits just to have a little bit more time with her before the story and battles start ramping up. Her joining the party is a little abrupt. Allannia joining is also abrupt but kind of ties in with the story better. Maybe a little back and forth between her and the other party members while traveling to the dungeon or something, so we can get to know her personality more, instead of just the devout servant of the king. I also wouldn't mind a little more world building early on about the dungeons and dungeon cores although leaving on the mystery/cliffhanger without knowing too much about what's going on was executed really well.
All in all, great job, wonderful demo!
